title_en: Zhou Changchun v. Chuang's China Investments Limited, Li Shiwei, Peng Zhenjie and Third Party Hunan Hanye Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. — dispute over liability for damaging company interests
ruling_gist_en: Where it can be proven that the company's organ legally authorized to represent the company in filing a lawsuit has essentially no possibility of filing a lawsuit, and it is meaningless for the plaintiff to fulfill the preliminary procedures, the court should not dismiss the lawsuit on the ground that the shareholder has not fulfilled the preliminary procedures stipulated in Article 151 of the Company Law.

full_text_en:
Zhou Changchun v. Chuang's China Investment Limited, Li Shiwei, and Peng Zhenjie, and Third Party Hunan Hanye Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. — dispute over liability for damage to company interests

Ruling Summary

Where it can be proven that the company organ legally entitled to represent the company in filing a lawsuit basically has no possibility of initiating a lawsuit, and it would be meaningless for the plaintiff to fulfill the pre-procedure, it is inappropriate to dismiss the lawsuit on the ground that the shareholder has not fulfilled the pre-procedure prescribed in Article 151 of the Company Law.

Supreme People's Court Civil Ruling
(2019) Zui Gao Fa Min Zhong No. 1679

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Zhou Changchun, female, born on April 17, 1962, Han Chinese, domiciled in Shunde District, Foshan City, Guangdong Province.

Agent ad litem: Ni Lianfu, lawyer at Beijing Tianchi Juntai Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Xu Boping, lawyer at Beijing Tianchi Juntai Law Firm.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Chuang's China Investment Limited, domiciled at 25th Floor, Alexandra House, 18 Chater Road, Central, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

Representative: Zhuang Jiabin, General Manager of the company.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Li Shiwei, male, born on January 19, 1937, domiciled at Tin Hau Temple Road, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Peng Zhenjie, male, born on October 4, 1957, domiciled at Heng Fa Chuen, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

Joint agent ad litem for the above three appellees: He Chuan, lawyer at Beijing King & Wood (Shenzhen) Law Firm.

Joint agent ad litem for the above three appellees: Liu Ding, lawyer at Beijing King & Wood (Shenzhen) Law Firm.

Third Party at First Instance: Hunan Hanye Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at Administrative Service Center, Muyun Industrial Park, left side of Nanhu Avenue, Changsha County, Hunan Province.

Legal Representative: Li Shiwei, Chairman of the company.

Agent ad litem: Song Siyu, lawyer at Beijing King & Wood (Shenzhen) Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Liu Chen, lawyer at Beijing King & Wood (Shenzhen) Law Firm.

Appellant Zhou Changchun appealed against the Civil Ruling (2017) Xiang Min Chu No. 18 of Hunan High People's Court to this Court regarding the dispute over liability for damage to company interests with appellees Chuang's China Investment Limited (hereinafter referred to as Chuang's China Company), Li Shiwei, Peng Zhenjie, and third party at first instance Hunan Hanye Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hunan Hanye Company). This Court accepted the case on September 10, 2019, and formed a collegial panel to hear the case in accordance with the law. The case is now concluded.

Appellant Zhou Changchun appealed to this Court with the following requests: to set aside the first-instance ruling and order Hunan High People's Court to hear this case. Facts and Reasons: (1) The first-instance court erred in finding facts by denying the authenticity of the Board Resolution of Hunan Hanye Company dated November 18, 2010 submitted by Zhou Changchun. 1. The Civil Judgment (2012) Chang Zhong Min Si Chu Zi No. 0590 of Changsha Intermediate People's Court (hereinafter referred to as Civil Judgment No. 0590) denied the authenticity of the Board Resolution, violating the provisions of the Supreme People's Court's Several Provisions on Evidence in Civil Proceedings regarding the determination of evidentiary validity. Zhou Changchun submitted the original Board Resolution and also submitted relevant documents of Hunan Hanye Company signed by Peng Zhenjie and Li Shiwei with acknowledged authenticity for comparison. A visual comparison showed high consistency in font, writing style, stroke order, and habits. The first-instance court relied on Civil Judgment No. 0590 to deny the authenticity of the Board Resolution and reject Zhou Changchun's application for handwriting expertise, thereby erroneously denying the procedural legality of Zhou Changchun's shareholder representative action, constituting an error in fact-finding. (2) The first-instance ruling held that, in the absence of a supervisor in Hunan Hanye Company, Zhou Changchun should file a lawsuit application with the board of directors of Hunan Hanye Company and could only initiate a shareholder representative action in her own name after the board refused, and found that Zhou Changchun's lawsuit without fulfilling the pre-procedure for shareholder representative action was unlawful, constituting an error in applying the law. 1. Under the system of shareholder representative action in Article 151 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China, where a company director infringes upon the company's interests, a company shareholder only needs to make a request to the board of supervisors or supervisor of the company, and there is absolutely no need to make a request to the company or its board of directors. The first-instance court's requirement that Zhou Changchun apply to Hunan Hanye Company or its board of directors to initiate a lawsuit, and could only file a shareholder representative action after Hunan Hanye Company or the board failed to do so, lacks legal basis. 2. The first-instance ruling asserted that the board of directors of Hunan Hanye Company has five directors, while the appellees (first-instance defendants) in this case are only two of them, and therefore an application to the board of directors of Hunan Hanye Company might result in the board filing a lawsuit. This argument is completely untenable. The annual report of Chuang's China Company submitted by Zhou Changchun already proves that, except for Zhou Changchun, the other four directors all hold senior positions in Chuang's China Company and have close interests. Therefore, the board of directors of Hunan Hanye Company has no possibility whatsoever of filing a lawsuit against the appellees for their infringing acts. The Supreme People's Court stated in its Civil Ruling (2015) Min Si Zhong Zi No. 54: "Where the internal organizational structure of the company has already malfunctioned, or where the company's directors or supervisors have caused losses to the company and are defendants in the case, the organ that expresses the company's intent (board of directors, board of supervisors) will not sue themselves in the company's name, and under such circumstances, the pre-procedure requirement for shareholder derivative actions should be exempted." Given that Hunan Hanye Company has not appointed a supervisor and that the directors and actual controllers of Hunan Hanye Company have damaged the company's interests, and considering that the board of directors controlled by the appellees will definitely not file a lawsuit, the pre-procedure for shareholders of Hunan Hanye Company to initiate a shareholder representative action should be exempted, allowing Zhou Changchun to directly file a shareholder representative action. Precedents show that the pre-procedure may be bypassed. Even if the pre-procedure were to be fulfilled, Zhou Changchun has already made an application to Zhou Yike, the supervisor of Hunan Hanye Company. Hunan Hanye Company is a joint venture, and the board of directors is the highest decision-making body of Hunan Hanye Company. Zhou Yike was appointed as the company's supervisor with the consent of five directors. The new evidence submitted by Zhou Changchun, the Consulting Opinion on Expertise from Beijing Jing'an Tuopu Document Forensic Examination Center, can prove that the signatures of directors Li Shiwei (Chairman), Peng Zhenjie, and Li Meixin on the board resolution of Hunan Hanye Company dated October 18, 2010 are genuine. Zhou Changchun submitted the original board resolution, which is complete in content. The new evidence submitted by Zhou Changchun is sufficient to overturn the facts established by the effective civil judgment.

Chuang's China Company, Li Shiwei, and Peng Zhenjie argued in defense: (1) The board resolution document submitted by Zhou Changchun contains obvious falsehoods, and both the Changsha Intermediate People's Court and the first-instance court have previously rendered judgments denying the authenticity of that board resolution. The first-instance ruling correctly applied the law and found the facts. Since the five directors of Hunan Hanye Company (who are also directors of New Era Investment Limited, the majority shareholder of Hunan Hanye Company with a 90% shareholding) have long been in different locations, the boards of directors of both companies often held meetings by telephone and then circulated board resolutions for signature. In fact, the board resolution submitted by Zhou Changchun should have been the signing page of the board resolution of New Era Investment Limited formed on November 28, 2009. That document was signed by Li Shiwei, Peng Zhenjie, and Li Meixin and then mailed to Fan Xiaohan. Due to a dispute, Fan Xiaohan never mailed the resolution document back to New Era Investment Limited. The forged board resolution submitted by Zhou Changchun has the following obvious defects: 1. The board resolution of New Era Investment Limited indicated "Four directors should attend, four directors actually attended," so only four signature spaces were left on page 2. On the forged board resolution, Zhou Changchun's signature was actually filled in by herself in a blank space. 2. Because the genuine document was a board resolution of New Era Investment Company, the signing page bore the seal of New Era Investment Limited. If it were a board resolution of Hunan Hanye Company, the seal of New Era Investment Limited would not have been affixed at all. (2) Zhou Changchun's filing of this lawsuit must be conditioned on exhausting internal remedies. The circumstances of this case do not apply to the opinions expressed by the Supreme People's Court in individual cases. According to clear statutory provisions and a large number of Supreme Court judicial precedents, Zhou Changchun's failure to fulfill the pre-procedure for a shareholder representative action constitutes a circumstance where the lawsuit should be dismissed. First, in the Supreme People's Court's (2015) Min Si Zhong Zi No. 54 case, it was emphasized that Article 151 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China establishes the pre-procedure for shareholder derivative actions. Second, the special circumstance in the Supreme People's Court's (2015) Min Si Zhong Zi No. 54 case was that the three directors of the company were respectively the plaintiff and defendants, so it was impossible for the board of directors to form a majority opinion to achieve rights relief. However, in this case, the board of directors of Hunan Hanye Company has five directors. Zhou Changchun sued Li Shiwei and Peng Zhenjie, but it was still possible to obtain support from Zhuang Xuenong and Li Meixin to form a majority board vote to initiate a lawsuit. Thus, Zhou Changchun clearly did not exhaust internal corporate remedies. Third, in the Supreme People's Court's (2015) Min Si Zhong Zi No. 54 case, the plaintiff had previously taken remedial measures such as filing a lawsuit in the name of the legal representative, which were dismissed. The judge in that case, based on the overall circumstances, found that the plaintiff had exhausted all remedies. Such circumstances do not exist in this case. Finally, that case is not a guiding case or a gazette case; it can only serve as a reference, not as the basis for determining this case. A large number of precedents emphasize that judicial intervention in corporate disputes should be limited. Before judicial power intervenes in corporate disputes, internal remedies must first be exhausted. Where shareholders can obtain relief by filing a lawsuit themselves, a representative action should not be brought. (3) Zhou Changchun deliberately circumvented the statutory pre-procedure requirements for shareholder representative actions, used forged documents, and colluded with Zhou Yike to fabricate the illusion that the pre-procedure had been fulfilled. Moreover, the substantive claims brought by Zhou Changchun also contain a large number of distortions, fabrications, and malicious inventions. Zhou Changchun is suspected of the crime of false litigation. In conclusion, the appellees requested that Zhou Changchun's appeal be dismissed and the original ruling be upheld.

Hunan Hanye Company stated: Zhou Yike has never been the supervisor of Hunan Hanye Company. The industrial and commercial filing materials of Hunan Hanye Company do not include the board resolution of Hunan Hanye Company dated November 18, 2010 submitted by Zhou Changchun, nor does any document of Hunan Hanye Company reflect that Zhou Yike performed the duties of a company supervisor. Zhou Changchun alleges that Li Shiwei, as the legal representative of Hunan Hanye Company, Peng Zhenjie, as the general manager of Hunan Hanye Company, and Chuang's China Company, as the actual controller of Hunan Hanye Company, jointly damaged the company's interests. This should be governed by Article 151, paragraph 3 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China, requiring the fulfillment of the pre-procedure for shareholder representative action with the board of directors of Hunan Hanye Company. Zhou Changchun, using a false board resolution document, maliciously circumvented the statutory pre-procedure and should be dismissed.

Zhou Changchun filed the following claims with the first-instance court: 1. Order Chuang's China Company, Li Shiwei, and Peng Zhenjie to jointly compensate Hunan Hanye Company RMB 7,508,250, plus interest calculated at the corresponding bank loan rate from October 8, 2005 until the compensation is fully paid (interest as of June 1, 2017 is tentatively calculated at RMB 5,702,011.15). 2. Order Chuang's China Company, Li Shiwei, and Peng Zhenjie to jointly compensate Hunan Hanye Company for economic losses of RMB 32,210,138.92 plus interest calculated at the corresponding bank loan rate from July 16, 2012 until the compensation is fully paid (interest as of June 1, 2017 is tentatively calculated at RMB 9,253,525.55). 3. Order Chuang's China Company, Li Shiwei, and Peng Zhenjie to compensate for economic losses of RMB 50,000,000 (the above economic losses are tentative estimates; the actual losses shall be determined by the court based on the actual losses caused to Hunan Hanye Company) caused by undervaluing and offsetting Hunan Hanye Company's assets and appropriating Hunan Hanye Company's business opportunities. 4. Order the litigation costs of the first instance to be borne by Chuang's China Company, Li Shiwei, and Peng Zhenjie.

The first-instance court found upon review: This case is a shareholder representative action brought by Zhou Changchun on behalf of Hunan Hanye Company. According to Article 151 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China: Where a director or senior manager falls under the circumstances specified in Article 149 of this Law, a shareholder of a limited liability company or a shareholder of a joint stock limited company who has held alone or together with other shareholders one percent or more of the company's shares for a consecutive period of 180 days or more may request, in writing, the board of supervisors or, in the case of a limited liability company without a board of supervisors, the supervisor to file a lawsuit with the people's court. Where a supervisor falls under the circumstances specified in Article 149 of this Law, the aforementioned shareholders may request, in writing, the board of directors or, in the case of a limited liability company without a board of directors, the executive director to file a lawsuit with the people's court. If the board of supervisors, the supervisor of a limited liability company without a board of supervisors, or the board of directors, the executive director refuses to file a lawsuit after receiving the written request from the shareholders as specified in the preceding paragraph, or fails to file a lawsuit within thirty days from the date of receiving the request, or if the circumstances are urgent and failure to file the lawsuit immediately would cause irreparable damage to the company's interests, the shareholders specified in the preceding paragraph have the right, in the company's interest, to directly file a lawsuit with the people's court in their own names. Where others infringe upon the company's lawful rights and interests and cause losses to the company, the shareholders specified in the first paragraph of this Article may file a lawsuit with the people's court in accordance with the provisions of the preceding two paragraphs. In this case, Zhou Changchun, representing Hunan Hanye Company in filing a lawsuit, must first fulfill the pre-procedure for shareholder representative action as prescribed in Article 151 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China. Zhou Changchun claimed that Hunan Hanye Company appointed Zhou Yike as the supervisor of Hunan Hanye Company. For this purpose, she submitted to this court the Board Resolution of Hunan Hanye Company dated November 18, 2010 and applied for an expertise on that Board Resolution to prove that Zhou Yike was the supervisor of Hunan Hanye Company. The first-instance court held that the Changsha Intermediate People's Court's Civil Judgment No. 0590 had already denied the authenticity of that Board Resolution. The effective Civil Judgment (2017) Xiang Min Zhong No. 636 of this court also affirmed the facts found in Civil Judgment No. 0590. According to Article 93 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, facts confirmed by an effective judgment of a people's court need not be proved by the parties. Therefore, the first-instance court did not permit Zhou Changchun's application for expertise on the Board Resolution dated November 18, 2010. Zhou Changchun also did not submit other evidence to prove that Zhou Yike was the supervisor of Hunan Hanye Company. Hence, the existing evidence cannot prove that Zhou Yike is the supervisor of Hunan Hanye Company. Consequently, Zhou Changchun's claim that she fulfilled the pre-procedure for shareholder representative action by making a written request to Zhou Yike and being refused is untenable. Zhou Changchun further argued that, since the directors and actual controller of Hunan Hanye Company would not sue themselves, it was impossible to require the company's shareholder to fulfill the pre-procedure for shareholder representative action at this time, and therefore the shareholder should be allowed to directly initiate a shareholder representative action. Even if Hunan Hanye Company does not recognize Zhou Yike as the company supervisor, it does not prevent Zhou Changchun, as a shareholder of Hunan Hanye Company, from filing a shareholder representative action to protect the company's interests. The first-instance court held that the board of directors of Hunan Hanye Company consists of five directors: Li Shiwei, Li Meixin, Peng Zhenjie, Zhuang Xuenong, and Zhou Changchun. Zhou Changchun, as the plaintiff at first instance, sued two of the directors, Li Shiwei and Peng Zhenjie. The board of directors might still form a majority vote to initiate a lawsuit. Moreover, Zhou Changchun not only sued the two directors Li Shiwei and Peng Zhenjie but also sued Chuang's China Company. According to Article 151, paragraph 3 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China, Zhou Changchun could also file a written request with the board of directors of Hunan Hanye Company to initiate a lawsuit. Only if the board refused or failed to file a lawsuit within thirty days could Zhou Changchun file this shareholder representative action. Therefore, the court did not support Zhou Changchun's direct initiation of a shareholder representative action without fulfilling the above pre-procedure. In summary, Zhou Changchun did not fulfill the statutory pre-procedure for initiating a shareholder representative action, and the objective circumstances of this case do not present the statutory situation of "urgency where irreparable loss would result." Zhou Changchun is not entitled to file a shareholder representative action under the above provisions. Given that Zhou Changchun is currently not entitled to file a shareholder representative action, her application for handwriting expertise on the authenticity of the signatures of Fan Xiaohan and Zhou Changchun on the Board Resolution of Hunan Hanye Company dated October 30, 2009 is also not allowed. The court, in accordance with Article 119 and Article 154, paragraph 1, item 3 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 208, paragraph 3 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, ruled: Zhou Changchun's lawsuit is dismissed.

During the second instance, Zhou Changchun submitted the Consulting Opinion on Expertise from Beijing Jing'an Tuopu Document Forensic Examination Center to prove the authenticity of the Board Resolution of Hunan Hanye Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. dated November 18, 2010. Chuang's China Company, Li Shiwei, Peng Zhenjie, and Hunan Hanye Company all denied the authenticity, legality, and relevance of this evidence.

This court finds upon trial: Hunan Hanye Company was registered and established in the Hunan Provincial Administration for Industry and Commerce in 2002, with a registered capital of RMB 10,000,000. The shareholders were Zhou Changchun and Fan Xiaohan (who were husband and wife). In 2004, with the approval of the Hunan Provincial People's Government, Hunan Hanye Company was converted into a limited liability company (joint venture with Taiwan, Hong Kong, and Macao and domestic parties), and its registered capital was increased to RMB 25,000,000. Among them, Zhou Changchun contributed RMB 2,500,000, holding a 10% share; New Era Investment Limited contributed RMB 22,500,000, holding a 90% share. Article 15 of the Articles of Association of the Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture of Hunan Hanye Company provides: The board of directors shall be composed of five directors, of which one shall be appointed by Zhou Changchun, and New Era Investment Limited shall appoint four. The chairman of the board shall be designated by New Era Investment Limited. On December 29, 2011, the legal representative of Hunan Hanye Company was changed from Fan Xiaohan to Li Shiwei. The board of directors of Hunan Hanye Company consists of Li Shiwei (Chairman), Peng Zhenjie, Zhuang Xuenong, Li Meixin, and Zhou Changchun. It is also found that the performance reports of Chuang's China Company for the fiscal years 2004 to 2017 state that Li Meixin, Peng Zhenjie, and Li Shiwei are directors of Chuang's China Company, and Zhuang Xuenong is a senior manager of Chuang's China Company.

This court holds that, in light of the appellant's grounds of appeal and the appellees' arguments in defense, the focus of the dispute in this case is whether the first-instance ruling dismissing Zhou Changchun's lawsuit is correct.

Article 151 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "Where a director or senior manager is in the circumstances as described in Article 149 of this Law, a shareholder of a limited liability company, or a shareholder of a joint stock limited company who individually or jointly holds one percent or more of the company's shares for a continuous period of 180 days or more, may request in writing the board of supervisors, or the supervisor of a limited liability company without a board of supervisors, to institute legal proceedings in the people's court; where a supervisor is in the circumstances as described in Article 149 of this Law, the aforesaid shareholder may request in writing the board of directors, or the executive director of a limited liability company without a board of directors, to institute legal proceedings in the people's court. If the board of supervisors, the supervisor of a limited liability company without a board of supervisors, the board of directors, or the executive director, after receiving the written request from the shareholder as prescribed in the preceding paragraph, refuses to institute legal proceedings, or fails to institute legal proceedings within thirty days from the date of receiving the request, or if the circumstances are urgent and failure to institute legal proceedings immediately would cause irreparable harm to the company's interests, the shareholder as prescribed in the preceding paragraph shall have the right to institute legal proceedings directly in the people's court in its own name for the benefit of the company. Where others infringe upon the lawful rights and interests of the company and cause losses to the company, the shareholder as prescribed in paragraph 1 of this Article may institute legal proceedings in the people's court in accordance with the provisions of the preceding two paragraphs." The shareholder's written request to the relevant organ of the company to institute legal proceedings in the people's court is a prerequisite procedure for the shareholder to bring a derivative action. Generally, if the shareholder fails to fulfill the prerequisite procedure, the lawsuit shall be dismissed. However, this prerequisite procedure is intended for the general situation of corporate governance, i.e., when the shareholder submits a written request to the relevant organ of the company, there exists the possibility that the relevant organ of the company will institute legal proceedings. If such possibility does not exist, the lawsuit shall not be dismissed on the ground that the plaintiff has not fulfilled the prerequisite procedure. Applied to the specific circumstances of this case, the analysis is as follows:

First, according to Article 151 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China, where a director or senior manager is in the circumstances as described in Article 149 of this Law, a shareholder of a limited liability company may request in writing the board of supervisors, or the supervisor of a limited liability company without a board of supervisors, to institute legal proceedings. In this case, Li Shiwei and Peng Zhenjie were directors of Hunan Hanye Company. Zhou Changchun brought a shareholder derivative action against Li Shiwei and Peng Zhenjie as defendants, and should have first requested in writing the board of supervisors or the supervisor of Hunan Hanye Company to institute legal proceedings. However, during the inquiry in the second instance, Hunan Hanye Company clearly stated that it had no supervisor or board of supervisors registered with the administrative authority for industry and commerce. Although Zhou Changchun asserted that Zhou Yike was the supervisor of Hunan Hanye Company, this fact had been negated by the effective civil judgment of another court in a separate case. Hunan Hanye Company explicitly denied that Zhou Yike was its supervisor, and the evidence submitted by Zhou Changchun in the second instance was insufficient to overturn the facts established by the effective civil judgment of the separate case. Based on the above facts, the evidence in this case cannot prove that Hunan Hanye Company had established a board of supervisors or appointed a supervisor. The prerequisite procedure for Zhou Changchun to bring a shareholder derivative action against the company's directors Li Shiwei and Peng Zhenjie was objectively impossible to fulfill.

Second, Article 151, paragraph 3 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "Where others infringe upon the lawful rights and interests of the company and cause losses to the company, the shareholder as prescribed in paragraph 1 of this Article may institute legal proceedings in the people's court in accordance with the provisions of the preceding two paragraphs." Zhuangshi China Company is not a director, supervisor, or senior manager of Hunan Hanye Company. Since Hunan Hanye Company does not have a board of supervisors or a supervisor, the prerequisite procedure for Zhou Changchun to bring a derivative action against Zhuangshi China Company should be to request the board of directors of Hunan Hanye Company to institute legal proceedings. However, according to the facts found, the board of directors of Hunan Hanye Company consisted of Li Shiwei (Chairman), Peng Zhenjie, Zhuang Xuenong, Li Meixin, and Zhou Changchun. Except for Zhou Changchun, the other four board members of Hunan Hanye Company were all directors or senior managers of Zhuangshi China Company and had an interest in Zhuangshi China Company. There was essentially no possibility that the board of directors of Hunan Hanye Company would institute legal proceedings against Zhuangshi China Company. Requiring Zhou Changchun to fulfill the prerequisite procedure for a shareholder derivative action against Zhuangshi China Company was no longer necessary.

This case is a dispute over liability for damage to company interests brought by Zhou Changchun, a shareholder of Hunan Hanye Company, on behalf of the company, naming Zhuangshi China Company, Li Shiwei, and Peng Zhenjie as defendants, seeking joint and several compensation from all three defendants at first instance. Considering the above circumstances comprehensively, this court holds that Zhou Changchun's ground of appeal that he may directly initiate this lawsuit without going through the prerequisite procedure for a shareholder derivative action is valid. The first-instance ruling to dismiss the lawsuit was improper and should be corrected.

In conclusion, Zhou Changchun's appeal is sustained. Pursuant to Article 171 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 332 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, it is ruled as follows:

1. The civil ruling (2017) Xiang Min Chu No. 18 of the Hunan High People's Court is vacated;

2. This case is hereby remanded to the Hunan High People's Court for trial.

This ruling is final.
